title: Global duration shock broadens into European FX stress
net_new_delta: EUR reached a 17-month low as European assets absorbed the combined pressure of high oil, inflation risk, political uncertainty and globally elevated sovereign yields; US 10Y briefly reached 5.34% before easing near 5.27%, while equities remained comparatively resilient.
assumptions_affected: near-term Fed expectations as sufficient rates-state proxy

evidence.finding: EUR fell to a 17-month low as European assets were pressured by higher oil, inflation and political uncertainty.
US 10Y briefly reached about 5.34%, highest since 2002, then eased near 5.27%; UK 30Y exceeded 6% and France 10Y approached 5%.
December Brent traded around/above $100 after China suspended October fuel exports outside Hong Kong and Macau.
European FX weakness reflects the combined rates, energy/inflation and political backdrop rather than a single Fed-policy channel.

conflicts: Softer US inflation reduced immediate Fed-hike expectations while long-end sovereign yields remain at multi-decade extremes.
Equities remain comparatively resilient despite severe duration stress.
Recovering Gulf crude exports conflict with tightening refined-product supply after China's export suspension.
unknown: Persistence of EUR weakness and >5% US 10Y yields
Causal weights among fiscal risk, term premium, energy inflation and political risk
confidence: HIGH on observed duration/FX broadening; MEDIUM on persistence and causal decomposition
next_decisive_check: Test whether EUR remains weak and DXY firm if US 10Y holds near/above 5% and Brent remains near/above $100 through the next official US labor release; measure EUR-duration and NQ-duration conditional-beta stability.

oracle.finding: Duration stress has broadened into European FX transmission; promote a cross-region duration/FX regime hypothesis and test EUR/USD and NQ conditional betas without retuning strategy parameters.

supermesh_x.finding: Fresh Reuters evidence coherently spans US/European sovereign rates, EUR/USD, oil and equities; preserve distinct rates, energy and political-risk channels and keep unavailable microstructure fields explicit.
